findings.what: `pageRange` defaults `totalPages` with `totalPages || 1` instead of `totalPages ?? 1`.
findings.why: Node style guide rule 12: prefer `??` over `||` for defaults because `||` also triggers on `0`, which `totalPages` can legitimately be — the guide's own bad-example (`const count = total || 0`) is this exact shape.
findings.fix: Change `normalizePageNumber(page, totalPages || 1)` to `normalizePageNumber(page, totalPages ?? 1)` on line 53 of `pageRange`.

verdicts.reasoning: The `totalPages || 1` guard is pre-existing logic carried over verbatim from the shared common/helpers/pagination-helper.js (see buildResultsLabel: `normalizePageNumber(pagination.page, pagination.totalPages || 1)`, git show a62945d:src/server/common/helpers/pagination-helper.js), which this stage (D8 in s05-app-shell.md) folds into the feature's own view-model per plan decision, not code freshly authored with a style choice. More importantly it is not a functional defect: normalizePageNumber (line 49-50) already treats any totalPages < 1 (including 0) by returning 1 outright — `totalPages < 1 ? 1 : Math.min(Math.max(page, 1), totalPages)`. Tracing both branches for totalPages=0: without the `|| 1` fallback, normalizePageNumber(page, 0) hits `0 < 1` and returns 1; with the fallback, normalizePageNumber(page, 1) computes Math.min(Math.max(page,1),1) which is also always 1. The two forms produce an identical result in the only case where the guide's `||` vs `??` distinction matters (0), so there is no behavioural difference to fix — it is stylistic-only on code that already exists elsewhere in the codebase, not a defect introduced by this diff.

findings.what: Reachability is computed into a separate `reachability` boolean array and then re-joined to `services` by numeric index (`services.filter((service, index) => !reachability[index])`).
findings.why: Node style rule 4 (prefer functional style) and rule 9 (avoid clever constructs at the expense of clarity) — parallel arrays correlated by index are a classic smell: nothing keeps the two arrays' lengths/order visibly tied together at the call site, so a future edit that reorders or filters one array before the other silently produces wrong `unreachable` results. Attaching the boolean directly to each service removes the implicit index contract.
findings.fix: Fold the reachable flag onto each service inside the same map so no index correlation is needed: `const checked = await Promise.all(services.map(async (service) => ({ ...service, reachable: await isReachable(service) })))` then `const unreachable = checked.filter((service) => !service.reachable)`.
